title: Physical and chemical conditions of molecular gas in NGC 1068: The nuclear feedback in the circumnuclear disk and starburst ring
question: Map the physical conditions across the circumnuclear disk and the starburst ring of NGC 1068, test whether the nuclear outflow influences the molecular gas in the ring, and examine whether the heating or the quiescent cloud scenario better matches the observations.

data.sensitivity: Channel noise after convolving to 0.8'': 0.41 to 0.82 mJy/beam

evidence.quote: Located at a distance of 14 Mpc ((cite: Bland1997); 1$''$ $\sim$ 70 pc), its proximity enables sufficient spatial resolution to distinguish between star formation and AGN-driven processes.
The rest frequencies were determined using the systemic velocity from (cite: Garcia2019), with $v_{sys}(HEL) \simeq$ 1130 km/s.

what.value: Linewidths of 150, 100, and 50 km s^-1 for the CND, stellar bar, and starburst ring

evidence.quote: We adopted linewidths of 150, 100, and 50 km s$^{-1}$ for the CND, stellar bar, and starburst ring, respectively (cite: Scourfield2020).

what.value: Superstar cluster (SSC) positions in the starburst ring

evidence.quote: The SSC positions are adopted from (cite: Villas2021), where Pa$\alpha$ emission was used to trace compact young stellar clusters.
Circles denote sub-regions in the CND and the AGN, squares indicate superstar clusters (SSCs) in the starburst ring, and a pentagram marks the position of Type II SN 2018ivc (cite: bostroem2020).

what.value: Previous physical parameter measurements (n_H2, T_K, zeta) in NGC 1068 sub-regions for comparison

evidence.quote: We compare our results with previous multi molecular studies of NGC 1068 in Fig. 6, focusing on (cite: Josh2022), (cite: viti2014), and (cite: Scourfield2020).

recipe.goal: Convolve cubes, generate moment-0 maps, and partition into hexagonal regions
recipe.method: Convolve all ALMA image cubes to a common 0.8'' beam, integrate over velocity windows to make moment-0 maps, and partition into 56 pc hexagonal regions keeping detections with S/N >= 3 and regions with >5 detected transitions.
key_parameters: Common beam = 0.8''; Hexagon size = 56 pc; S/N threshold >= 3; > 5 detected transitions per hexagon (198 regions total)
Velocity integration windows: |v - v_sys| <= 230 km s^-1 for most transitions; v - v_sys in [-510, 230] km s^-1 for C2H (1-0)

recipe.goal: Generate chemical model grid and train neural network emulator
recipe.method: Run two-stage UCLCHEM models (both quiescent and heating scenarios) across a 4D parameter grid, filter out abundances < 10^-15, normalize to (-1, 1), and train a 4-hidden-layer TensorFlow neural network to predict fractional molecular abundances.
key_parameters: 4 inputs: T_K in [30, 300] K (26 log points), n_H2 in [10^3, 10^7] cm^-3 (23 log points), zeta in [1, 10^3] zeta_0 (31 log points), N_H2 in [10^22, 10^25] cm^-2 (26 log points); 481,988 unique combinations
Architecture: 4 hidden layers with 2048 nodes each, ReLU activation, MSE loss, early stopping after 20 epochs without validation loss improvement; 80%/10%/10% train/val/test split
assumptions: Stage 1 freefall collapse from n = 100 cm^-3, T = 10 K, zeta_0 = 1.3e-17 s^-1 over 6 Myr; Stage 2 evolution for 1 Myr at fixed visual extinction A_v = 10 mag

recipe.goal: Perform hierarchical Bayesian inference coupled with non-LTE radiative transfer
recipe.method: Couple neural network chemical abundances with SpectralRadex non-LTE radiative transfer to predict line ratios, and sample the hierarchical Bayesian posterior across 198 hexagonal regions using Nautilus for both heating and quiescent models.
key_parameters: Observables: m = n - 1 chained log line ratios y_i^obs = ln(r_i) where r_k = I_k / I_{k+1}; Linewidths = 150, 100, and 50 km s^-1 for CND, stellar bar, and starburst ring
Hyperparameter priors: mu_n in (3.0, 6.00), mu_T in (1.55, 2.30), mu_N in (22.5, 24.0), mu_zeta in (0.0, 2.0), sigma_error in (0.02, 0.5)
assumptions: All transitions optically thin at best-fit parameters; C2H (N=1-0) modeled as a single transition; ensemble of region parameters follows a multivariate Student-t distribution with soft correlation bounds

recipe.goal: Extract and fit CO(1-0) and 13CO(1-0) line profiles
recipe.method: Extract CO(1-0) and 13CO(1-0) spectra from selected regions in the CND, arcs, and inner edges of the starburst ring and fit single-component Gaussian profiles to test for non-Gaussian outflow wings and multiple kinematic components.
key_parameters: Single-component Gaussian FWHM values in SSC1, SSC2, SSC3 and N-SB-Bar regions

score_reason: Archival ALMA project codes, target transitions, velocity integration windows, hexagonal binning tool (HERA), and Bayesian prior ranges are clearly specified, and all core underlying packages (UCLCHEM, SpectralRadex, Nautilus, TensorFlow) are public. However, CASA imaging details, the trained neural network emulator weights, the exact hierarchical Bayesian likelihood script, and the provenance of the CO/13CO cubes are not provided.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the software stack (CASA, HERA, UCLCHEM, TensorFlow, SpectralRadex, Nautilus) is open-source, and the main results are concrete regional statistics (mean n_H2, T_kin, N_H2, zeta, and Bayes factors) that can be quantitatively compared.
